gen-dafont-starborn-gf-bree-serif: Dreamy letters drifting apart, with whole skies between them. Starborn does its finest work in a few large words, its dark lowercase stripe floating in space, while Bree Serif settles underneath with oversized lowercase.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-quando: Starry, spacious, almost weightless. Starborn works best as a word or two set large, where its dark lowercase band can glow, while Quando adds a bookish, traditional serif voice with wide, sparse spacing.
gen-dafont-starborn-space-grotesk: Dreamy, widely spaced Starborn runs a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through each line, while its strokes barely vary. Space Grotesk's geometric, constant-width strokes keep paragraphs moving along smoothly.
gen-dafont-stencilia-fs-plein: Structural and striking, Stencilia leaves spacious gaps at its curve terminals and keeps its lowercase tightly close to the ascender line. Plein then reads steadily, reliable and clean, paragraph after paragraph.
gen-dafont-stencilia-fs-spline-sans: Stencilia packs its lowercase close under the ascender line, with generous gaps opening at every curve terminal. Spline Sans brings a moderate lowercase height and uniform strokes, which is where the pair really separates.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-quando: Quando reads bookish and traditional, its serif letters spaced wide and sparse around a big middle zone. And Stencilia heads the page with structural, striking letters, open at the curve ends.
gen-dafont-stencilia-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk draws geometric, constant-width letters with counters that breathe. Stencilia's structural, high-set lowercase against that moderate one is where the pair differs most, and it is striking.
gen-dafont-stentiga-fs-plein: Spread out, luxurious, and in no hurry at all. Stentiga's refined, widely tracked, high-set letters lead up top, and Plein follows with reliable, clean lowercase of moderate height.
gen-dafont-true-north-fs-hind: Contemporary and bold, with curves that never quite close. Hind is the one with steady strokes and lowercase nearly matching its capitals, while True North's stocky lines do the shouting.
gen-dafont-true-north-fs-quicksand: True North's curves refuse to close, and its stocky middle band makes every line feel bold. And Quicksand traces each letter in a line of constant weight, with bowls like blown glass, for the quieter reading work.
